glossary.Prokaryote: A cell lacking a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles (bacteria, archaea).
glossary.Eukaryote: A cell with a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.
glossary.Mitochondrion: Double-membraned organelle that carries out aerobic respiration and produces most ATP.
glossary.Fluid mosaic model: Model of the membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins, cholesterol, and carbohydrates.
glossary.Osmosis: Diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane toward higher solute concentration.
glossary.Sodium-potassium pump: Primary active transporter pumping 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per ATP.
glossary.ATP: Adenosine triphosphate, the cell's main energy currency.
glossary.Glycolysis: Cytosolic splitting of glucose into 2 pyruvate, net 2 ATP and 2 NADH.
glossary.Citric acid cycle: Mitochondrial cycle producing 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP, and 2 CO2 per turn.
glossary.Oxidative phosphorylation: ATP synthesis on the inner mitochondrial membrane driven by an electron transport chain and chemiosmosis; oxygen is the final electron acceptor.
glossary.Codon: A three-nucleotide unit of mRNA specifying an amino acid or stop signal; 64 exist.
glossary.Start codon: AUG, which codes for methionine and sets the reading frame.
glossary.Stop codons: UAA, UAG, and UGA, which terminate translation.
glossary.Semiconservative replication: DNA replication in which each daughter helix keeps one parental strand.
glossary.Okazaki fragments: Short DNA segments synthesized on the lagging strand, later joined by ligase.
glossary.Law of segregation: Mendel's principle that the two alleles of a gene separate into different gametes.
glossary.Km (Michaelis constant): The substrate concentration at which reaction velocity is half of Vmax; inversely related to affinity.
glossary.Competitive inhibitor: An inhibitor that binds the active site, raising apparent Km without changing Vmax.
glossary.Mitosis: Division producing two identical diploid cells via prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase.
glossary.Meiosis: Two divisions producing four genetically varied haploid gametes.
glossary.RuBisCO: Enzyme that fixes CO2 onto RuBP in the Calvin cycle (stroma).
glossary.Calvin cycle: Light-independent reactions in the stroma that fix carbon into G3P using ATP and NADPH.
glossary.Resting membrane potential: The neuron's resting voltage, about -70 mV, inside negative relative to outside.
glossary.Action potential: An all-or-none depolarization-repolarization event triggered at threshold (about -55 mV).
glossary.Second messenger: An intracellular signaling molecule (e.g., cyclic AMP, Ca2+) that amplifies a signal.

rules.8989417aa0e745b7ad64666e53534f8a: Distinguish per-turn versus per-glucose yields, prokaryotic versus eukaryotic cells, meiosis I versus II, and similar levels. Do not conflate them.
